answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy anchors every identity in a willow graph grown from its own genesis transaction: each answer requires a walk that lets a cursor wander through branches the agent itself minted, and rewards are refracted through a prism that pays by graph depth instead of by answer count. A clone farm must grow every separate root because branches cannot be grafted across addresses, so cost scales super-linearly with headcount rather than splitting across clones.
